protocol.name: bead_layer_promote_v1

description.summary: Compositor-owned floating presentation of a layer surface

protocol.description: This optional protocol retains an existing wl_surface, its buffer tree and its immutable layer-shell role. The compositor switches its presentation between a docked layer and an undecorated floating surface. Exactly one presentation owns the surface in any frame, including screen capture. Coordinates are logical, after buffer transform and viewport mapping.

entry.name: invalid_surface
entry.summary: Surface has no live layer-shell role

description.summary: Destroy the manager without affecting existing controllers

request.name: get_promotion

description.summary: Control the presentation of an existing layer root

request.description: The root must have a live layer-shell role. A controller may be obtained before the root has its first buffer, including while an output is being removed. A closing layer's normal close event still applies; creating a controller does not make an unavailable output usable. Destroying the layer role invalidates its controller. The client must destroy that controller before obtaining another for a new role.

interface.name: bead_layer_promote_v1

description.summary: Atomic layer-to-floating ownership and interactive movement

interface.description: Promote, dock and cancel are double-buffered with the root wl_surface commit; the last staged request wins. Request serials are client-owned monotonic uints compared with signed wraparound differences. Stale or duplicate serials are ignored. Move is immediate. Configure and rejected acknowledge requests; there is no configure acknowledgement request. Null-buffer commits cancel staged requests and end floating presentation. The controller remains reusable on remap. Controller destruction restores docked ownership. A client must not attach an xdg role or create a second content surface for this handoff. The compositor supplies placement, pointer movement, focus, output migration and transition animation.

entry.name: invalid_geometry
entry.summary: Invalid body rectangle or command grab arguments

request.name: promote

description.summary: Float the current layer content at its current position

request.description: The body rectangle is surface-local and identifies the visible window geometry within the existing surface. It does not resize the buffer. Width and height must be positive and no greater than 32768 logical units; the body must fit the mapped surface at commit. Geometry that does not fit the current buffer is rejected without changing ownership. The compositor derives global placement from its current layer position. A mapped root keeps its previous compositor pose even if pending layer geometry changes accompany this commit. A root's first content commit instead uses its newly committed layer placement, allowing restoration of saved positions without creating a second content surface. A non-null seat requires a current pointer button grab on this surface and its button press serial. At commit the compositor preserves the grab point and includes movement since that press, then moves the content immediately as the pointer moves. Motion, relative motion and the final button release remain delivered to the client. An expired or unrelated grab is rejected. For command-driven promotion, seat must be null and button_serial must be zero. Promotion of an already promoted surface is rejected. Clients keep their root buffer coordinates stable while promoted; compositor geometry events report global placement.

request.name: move

description.summary: Start another move of promoted content

request.description: The same seat, surface and current button serial validation as promote applies. No root commit is required. Invalid moves emit rejected using the last accepted request serial and leave presentation unchanged.

request.name: dock

description.summary: Restore layer ownership on the current promoted output

request.description: The compositor animates the retained content to its layer-shell anchor on the current output using its layer motion presentation sampler. The client may stage its docked scene with the same root commit. There is no buffer unmap/remap or second content surface in the handoff.

request.name: cancel

description.summary: Return to the original docked output and anchor

request.description: Behaves as dock but uses the original output if it still exists. If it was removed, the current surviving output is used. Docking or cancelling an already docked surface is rejected without side effects.

request.name: set_body_size

description.summary: Update promoted content extent with a new root buffer

request.description: Double-buffered with the root commit. Width and height must be positive, at most 32768 logical units, and fit the newly committed root texture at the original body origin. The body origin and pointer hotspot remain unchanged. The compositor reports the new extent using the active promotion serial. This request has no effect while docked or unmapped. It lets a client render its natural extent on the retained root after promotion, including content previously clipped by layer arrangement. No layer role recreation, resize handshake or second content surface is required. Clients retain their configured layer extent for docking.

event.name: configure

description.summary: Committed state or compositor movement notification

event.description: Rectangle coordinates describe the global visible body. Output is the compositor's output name. Moving notifications reuse the promotion serial and do not require client buffer commits. Docked reports the terminal anchor even while the compositor animates the return.

event.name: rejected
event.description: Reasons are human-readable diagnostics, not stable machine tokens.
